fields.meta_title: Parent Consent Form Builder for Schools and Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a parent consent form families sign on a phone, with the dates it covers and the medical details staff check. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Parent Consent Form Staff Can Check on the Spot
fields.hero_description: Create a parent consent form parents sign on their phones, plus a roster that coaches and nurses check before each activity.
fields.features_heading: What a Parent Consent Form Has to Settle
fields.features_subheading: Staff open these forms when they need an answer fast: a coach at the pool, a nurse with a sick student at the door.
fields.feature_1:
The child and what they may do

Ask for the child's name and date of birth, then the parent or guardian signing and how they are related. Name the activity and its dates. The form then records one clear decision.
fields.feature_2:
Consent with a start and an end

Set the dates a consent covers, such as one away meet or one school year. A form past its end date shows as expired on the roster, and the parent gets a link to sign again.
fields.feature_3:
Other adults a parent trusts

Let a parent list the grandparent or nanny who may pick the child up or bring them to a visit. Staff check a name against that list before the child leaves with any adult.
fields.feature_4:
Medical details staff can act on

Collect allergies and current medicines in their own fields, with a yes or no on emergency care if no parent answers the phone. The nurse or coach reads those answers first.
fields.feature_5:
Both parents, when the activity needs it

Send a second link to the other parent when an activity calls for two signatures. The form stays pending until both have signed, and each signature is saved with its own timestamp.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can host anywhere

On paid plans, export the consent app's source code to your GitHub repository. A district or league developer can host it on its own servers or link it to tools already in use.

fields.tab_content_1:
Consent that ends when the meet does

Harbor Swim Club drives 14 swimmers to the Lakeside Invitational. Each parent's form names that meet and the adult their child rides with. The coach's roster pairs every swimmer with a driver. When the meet ends on Sunday, each consent closes, and the next away meet needs new signatures.
fields.tab_content_2:
Adults named by a parent, matched at the front desk

Parents at Maple Pediatrics list up to 3 other adults who may bring their child in and give consent to routine care. When a grandmother checks in 6-year-old Leo, the front desk sees her name on his list. An adult who is not on it waits while staff call a parent.
fields.tab_content_3:
The student applies and a parent finishes

High school juniors apply to a summer course at Ridgeview College and enter a parent's email. That parent gets a link to the form with the course and class times already filled in. Registration holds every student under 18 until a parent signs. This week, 9 of 52 applicants are waiting.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each service a parent allowed, on the nurse's screen

At Lincoln Middle's health center, the parent form lists 5 services, each with its own box. Ana's mother ticked 3 of them, sick visits included. When Ana walks in with a sore throat, the nurse sees those 3 ticks before the visit starts. Every form renews in August for the new school year.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Parent Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a parent consent form around one decision and an end date, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Identify the child and the signer
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give the consent an end date
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write one sentence that says what the parent allows, such as riding to an away meet with another family or routine care at a school clinic. Every field on the form supports that sentence. Anything outside it belongs on a separate form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect the child's legal name and birthday. Ask how the signer is related to the child, and add a phone number that works on the day itself. A guardian who is not a parent can upload the court order that names them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set when the consent starts and when it stops, whether that is one weekend or one school year. Staff can then tell at a glance if it still applies, and a parent never wonders what a form signed two years ago still allows.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Include only what a coach or nurse would act on during the activity. A question nobody reads on the day is one more reason a parent stops halfway through. Put the doctor's phone number where staff can find it fast.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your wording into the prompt, then say who signs and when the consent ends. Emergent builds the form and the roster staff check, with a signature field at the bottom. Change any question later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick who gets an email or a Slack message when a parent signs, and who can open the medical fields. A coach may need the driver list for a trip without ever seeing a child's medicines.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form on a phone as a made-up family, sign it, then open the roster as staff. When a school or league supplies required wording, copy it exactly. Have a lawyer read any form that also waives rights.

faq_plan.q: What is a parent consent form?
faq_plan.a: A parent consent form is a signed record that a parent or guardian allows one specific thing for their child, such as a ride to an away meet or care at a school health center. It names the child and the adult who signs, then the activity and the dates the consent covers.

faq_plan.q: How to make a consent form for parents?
faq_plan.ref: How to make a consent form for parents?

prov.original: How to make a consent form for parents?

faq_plan.a: Decide what the parent is allowing and the last day it applies, then describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. Emergent builds the parents consent form and the database behind it. Paste in any wording a school or league requires, word for word.

faq_plan.q: What should a parental consent form include?
faq_plan.a: A parental consent form needs the child's full name and age, the signer and how they are related, the activity and its dates, and a phone number that works that day. Place the sentence that grants permission directly above the signature line. The parent then signs under exactly what they agree to.

faq_plan.q: When does a camp or school need a consent to treat minor form?
faq_plan.a: Use a consent to treat minor form when staff may have to arrange medical care while no parent can be reached, such as at an overnight camp. List the adults allowed to arrange that care, with the child's doctor. For a day outing where parents stay reachable, a field trip permission slip with an emergency number may cover it. Ask the school or district what it requires.

faq_plan.q: How long should a parent consent form for travel stay valid?
faq_plan.a: Only as long as the trip. Give the form a start date and an end date that match the travel dates, and ask for a new signature before the next trip. When one consent has to cover a school year instead, end it on the last day of school.

faq_plan.q: How do I get both parents to sign one parent consent form?
faq_plan.a: Ask the first parent for the other parent's email inside the form. The second link then goes out as soon as the first signature lands. Emergent can build in an email reminder for any link still unsigned after 3 days. Ask for two signatures only on activities that call for them.

faq_plan.q: How do I send a parent consent form to a whole team at once?
faq_plan.a: Send one link to the whole parent list and ask each parent to enter their child's name first. Every reply then lands on one roster, whichever parent filled it in. Adult chaperones and volunteer drivers sign a separate consent form for themselves, because no parent signs on their behalf.

faq_plan.q: How do staff check a parent consent form on the day of an activity?
faq_plan.a: Staff open the roster instead of the forms. Each child's row shows whether a parent signed and whether the consent still covers today, next to the adult the child leaves with. The form and the roster share one database you own, and nobody compares two lists at the gate.

faq_plan.q: Can I collect a minor consent form signature on a parent's phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Apps built with Emergent can capture e-signatures, and a parent signs with a finger on the phone screen. When a school or agency supplies the wording, ask whether it accepts an electronic signature before you retire its paper version.

faq_plan.q: Should a parent consent form also include a liability waiver?
faq_plan.a: Keep them apart. A parent consent form records what a parent allows, while a waiver asks the parent to give up claims, and that wording deserves its own section and a lawyer's read. A studio that works on clients under 18 can add a parent signature to its permanent makeup consent form the same way.

findings.quote: For a day outing where parents stay reachable, a field trip permission slip with an emergency number is enough.
findings.issue: States as fact what suffices for medical authorization of a minor on an outing (a legal and professional-standard question that varies by state, district and program). spec.domain_sources is empty and plan.claims_to_source lists nothing, so the claim has no source. Whole page searched for the same class (unsourced statements about law or medical consent): this is the only instance; the waiver line in FAQ 10 is a plain definition and the rest are recommendations.
findings.fix: Drop the sufficiency claim or turn it into advice, e.g. 'For a day outing where parents stay reachable, a field trip permission slip with an emergency number may cover it; ask the school or district what it requires for medical care.' Or source it in domain_sources from a primary authority and keep the wording to what the source says.

findings.quote: Parent consent form: the confirmation a parent sees after signing on a phone, with a button that opens the roster staff check.
findings.issue: The cover (and the same card drawn on the share image) gives the parent a 'View the roster' button. Everywhere else the roster is a staff tool with restricted medical fields: hero 'a roster that coaches and nurses check', step 06 'who can open the medical fields... A coach may need the driver list for a trip without ever seeing a child's medicines', FAQ 8 'Staff open the roster'. A parent opening the roster of every child's consent contradicts the page. Instances: cover.button 'View the roster', cover.alt, og card (rendered with 'View the roster').
findings.fix: Keep the parent view and change the button to something a parent does, e.g. 'View my consent' or 'Done', with alt 'the confirmation a parent sees after signing on a phone'; or recast the cover as the staff roster and rewrite the alt to match. Re-render cover and og.
